subject: First timer setting up a SEM: not only with lavaan, but ever

messages.author: bcb450677be3c338
messages.subject: First timer setting up a SEM: not only with lavaan, but ever
parts:
Dear all

I am not used to SEM at all, but for the first time I think that is a great way to analyze my data from an experiment. 

Here are the variables that I think should go into the model.

a) outcome: my dependent variable (binary)
b) treatment: my treatment variable (binary)
c) ssb: a latent that I cannot measure
d) exp1, exp2, exp3: three continuous measures that give me a hunch about ssb and so you would call them "manifest" I think.

Here are the relations that I think should go into the SEM.

1) treatment has an effect on exp1, exp2, exp3 and also on outcome.
2) exp1, exp2, exp3 manifest ssb.
3) ssb has an effect on outcome
4) exp1, exp2, exp3 are highly correlated


So I set up the following model:

# regressions
       outcome ~ ssb + treatment
       exp1 ~ treatment
       exp2 ~ treatment
       exp3 ~ treatment 

# latent variable definitions 
       ssb =~ treatment 
  
# residual variances and covariances 
       exp1 ~~ exp2
       exp1 ~~ exp3
       exp2 ~~ exp3

# intercepts

When I fit this model, I get two warning messages. 

***
Warning messages:
1: In lav_data_full(data = data, group = group, cluster = cluster,  :
  lavaan WARNING: some observed variances are (at least) a factor 1000 times larger than others; use varTable(fit) to investigate
2: In lav_model_vcov(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  :
  lavaan WARNING: could not compute standard errors!
  lavaan NOTE: this may be a symptom that the model is not identified.
***

While the first message seems to be cause by the nature of the variables (binary variables having the small variances), I cannot wrap my head around the second warning message.

Do you have any clue on how to improve this model? Thanks for the help.

messages.author: ee65f9feb643484e
messages.subject: Re: First timer setting up a SEM: not only with lavaan, but ever
parts:
Suggestions:

Use argument ordered="outcome". See http://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/cat.html

Leave out the residual covariances at first. I think that having them between all three pairs of exp variables is likely to cause trouble.

Having ssb ~ treatment would be more common (in my experience) than having exp1, exp2 and exp3 depend on treament directly, but it's hard to comment on this when I don't know your subject area.

Providing a reproducible example would make it easier for people to help you.

messages.author: ad188126f9138663
messages.subject: Re: First timer setting up a SEM: not only with lavaan, but ever
parts:
Sven,
  The warning says the following:
1: In lav_data_full(data = data, group = group, cluster = cluster,  :
lavaan WARNING: some observed variances are (at least) a factor 1000 times larger than others; use varTable(fit) to investigate

Did you follow the suggestion?  Is the ratio of the variances of one or more pairs of variables large?  If so, the warning is telling you that you need to rescale your variables to facilitate effective estimation.  The need for comparable scaling is discussed in most introductory SEM texts such as Rex Kline's book (4th edition, pages 81-82).

Keith

messages.author: bcb450677be3c338
messages.subject: Re: First timer setting up a SEM: not only with lavaan, but ever
parts:
Hi all

I have now rescaled variables exp1 and exp2 by dividing them by 1000. Now the scales of those two and exp3 are much more comparable. Thanks Keith!

I also added [ordered = "outcome"] as option to sem() because outcome is a categorical variable. Thanks Mark! 

The model now nicely converges and I get an interpretable output. 

Thanks for the help!
